- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### 108. 1989 — HM Land Registry — WA513690

Event id: ghf-19891010-1 · Date: 1989-10-10

On 10 October 1989 BP sells Oakview (title WA513690). How this land relates to the two parcels is unclear.

- **CONVEYANCER**: BP Properties sells Oakview, title WA513690.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: We need to plot that title against the farm boundaries.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki — Master Timeline (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/); Great House Farm Wiki — Land Registry Titles (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings)

### 109. 1989 — Vale of Glamorgan Planning

Event id: ghf-19891107-1 · Date: 1989-11-07

In October–November 1989 BP lodges outline application 89/01396/OUT for housing. The planning report records that buildings the Local Plan said should be kept had already been demolished. Outline permission follows on 13 March 1990, with 18 conditions.

- **PLANNING OFFICER**: The buildings the Local Plan wanted kept have already gone.
- **COUNCILLOR**: Then there is nothing left to protect but the ground.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### 110. 1989 — GGAT — Consultee Report

Event id: ghf-19891108-1 · Date: 1989-11-08

In its report on BP's outline application, GGAT advises that the application should not be decided without an archaeological assessment, specifies the trenching, prices the work at £2,000 over two weeks, and discloses negotiations with BP's agents. BP then commissions GGAT to do the work. The same report describes the farmhouse as having been listed as a 'county treasure'.

- **GGAT**: Assessment needed: machine trenching, two weeks, about two thousand pounds.
- **FAMILY**: The adviser to the council became the contractor to BP in the same breath.
- Source: GGAT — Forensic Review v4.0.3 (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/); Redevelopment (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/)

### 111. 1990 — Vale of Glamorgan Planning

Event id: ghf-19900208-1 · Date: 1990-02-08

On 8 February 1990 GGAT sends further comments on the outline application (Appendix B). They are missing from the planning file.

- **PLANNING CLERK**: The file refers to further GGAT comments as Appendix B.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: But Appendix B is not in the file we were given.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki — Master Timeline (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/); Great House Farm Wiki — Redevelopment and Church View Close (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/)

### 112. 1990 — Vale of Glamorgan Planning

Event id: ghf-19900313-1 · Date: 1990-03-13

On 13 March 1990 outline permission is granted with 18 conditions, including archaeological access, evaluation and mitigation. The officer's report had noted that the Local Plan said the farm buildings should be retained, but 'they were unfortunately demolished a little while ago'. No building preservation notice had ever been served.

- **PLANNING OFFICER**: The buildings should be retained. However, they were unfortunately demolished a little while ago.
- **FAMILY**: The plan said keep them. BP knocked them down first, and the council moved on.
- Source: Redevelopment (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/); Legal Review, section 4.4 (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/#criticism-register)

### 113. 1990 — GGAT Field Evaluation

Event id: ghf-19900801-1 · Date: 1990-08-01

In August 1990 GGAT digs eight machine trenches for BP. The eastern area 'could not be investigated', yet is zoned low potential. Early-medieval burials are found.

- **GGAT ARCHAEOLOGIST**: Eight trenches. The eastern area could not be investigated.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: So how could it be called low potential?
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### 114. 1990 — Vale of Glamorgan Planning

Event id: ghf-19901015-1 · Date: 1990-10-15

On 15 October 1990 the council records condition 17, the archaeological evaluation, as complied with, on the strength of GGAT's eight-trench evaluation of August.

- **ARCHIVIST**: Ground that could not be investigated was signed off as low potential.
- **FAMILY**: And four years later the burials were found right there.
- Source: Redevelopment (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/)

### 115. 1991 — Glamorgan-Gwent HER

Event id: ghf-19910821-1 · Date: 1991-08-21

The Glamorgan-Gwent Historic Environment Record compiles its official record of Great House Farm (PRN 02038s), synthesising archaeological assessments, the RCAHMW Inventory, and the supplementary notes of R.F. Sugget. This is followed by the first related archaeological event — an assessment of land at Great House Farm in 1990 (GGATE000877). The HER record will become the definitive archaeological account of the site, independently corroborating the demolition and documenting eight centuries of history.

- **HER COMPILER**: PRN 02038s is now compiled. It records eight centuries of history at Great House Farm.
- **ARCHAEOLOGICAL ASSESSOR**: Land at Great House Farm: an archaeological assessment is commissioned for 1990.
- **HER COMPILER**: The record cross-references the RCAHMW Inventory Vol IV Part 2 and seven related events through 2013.
- **HER OFFICER**: This official record independently corroborates the demolition on 6 December 1988.
- Source: GGAT HER PRN 02038s — Compiled 21-08-1991; GGATE000877: Great House Farm Archaeological Assessment (1990)

### 116. 1992 — Vale of Glamorgan Planning

Event id: ghf-19920514-1 · Date: 1992-05-14

On 14 May 1992 Ideal Homes Wales applies for approval of 20 detached houses on the farm site (92/00671/RES), more than a year before BP transfers the land to it.

- **IDEAL HOMES WALES**: Twenty detached houses, on the former farm site.
- **ARCHIVIST**: Applied for before the land had been transferred. On what interest?
- Source: Redevelopment (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/)

### 117. 1992 — Llandough

Event id: ghf-19920515-1 · Date: 1992-05-15

William (Billy) Buckler dies at Llandough Hospital on 15 May 1992 after a heart attack. He is buried at Michaelston-le-Pit after a funeral at Bethesda Chapel, Dinas Powys. He had been born in the farmhouse and defended it to the end.

- **FAMILY**: Billy was born in that house and fought for it all his life. He did not live to see the truth come out.
- **FAMILY**: We carry on for him.
- Source: The Williams / Buckler Family (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/)

### 118. 1992 — GGAT

Event id: ghf-19920727-1 · Date: 1992-07-27

On 27 July 1992 GGAT warns the council that the 1990 assessment showed significant archaeological deposits, including medieval and possibly earlier material and human bone, and urges mitigation. Page 2 of the letter is missing from the file.

- **GGAT**: Significant deposits, including human bone. Mitigation is needed.
- **ARCHIVIST**: And the second page of that warning is gone.
- Source: GGAT — Forensic Review v4.0.3, Test 9 (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/)

### 119. 1992 — Vale of Glamorgan Planning

Event id: ghf-19920903-1 · Date: 1992-09-03

On 3 September 1992, 38 days after GGAT's warning, the reserved matters for 20 houses are approved with no new archaeological condition. GGAT then records no act on the site for 466 days.

- **COUNCIL**: Reserved matters approved.
- **FAMILY**: Thirty-eight days after the warning about human bone. No new condition.
- Source: Redevelopment (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/); GGAT — Forensic Review v4.0.3 (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/)

### 120. 1993 — Former Farm Site

Event id: ghf-19931203-1 · Date: 1993-12-03

On 3 December 1993 BP transfers the site to Ideal Homes, and groundworks begin before the archaeological condition has been met.

- **SITE FOREMAN**: Groundworks start Monday.
- **GGAT ARCHAEOLOGIST**: Not before the archaeological condition is met.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### 121. 1993 — GGAT / Vale of Glamorgan

Event id: ghf-19931213-1 · Date: 1993-12-13

On 13 December 1993, with groundworks already under way, GGAT recommends urgent consideration of a breach-of-condition notice, saying condition 18 has not been fulfilled. The developer relies on counsel's opinion that it has been discharged, and the council accepts that, later telling the MP it was 'a difference of opinion'.

- **GGAT**: Condition 18 has not been fulfilled. A breach notice should be considered urgently.
- **COUNCIL**: A difference of opinion.
- Source: Redevelopment (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/); Legal Review, section 4.4 (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/#criticism-register)

### 122. 1994 — Cemetery Excavation, Former Farm Site

Event id: ghf-19940421-1 · Date: 1994-04-21

From 21 April to at least 3 May 1994 the Home Office licence to remove human remains has lapsed while work goes on. On 28 April GGAT's officer orders the excavation contractor to do 'no further work' until a brief is approved; under what authority is still unidentified. Removing remains without a licence was an offence under the Burial Act 1857.

- **GGAT OFFICER**: No further work until the brief is approved.
- **ARCHIVIST**: The licence had lapsed. What was lifted in those days, and on whose say-so?
- Source: GGAT — Forensic Review v4.0.3, Tests 8 and 10 (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/)

### 123. 1994 — Cemetery Excavation, Former Farm Site

Event id: ghf-19940504-1 · Date: 1994-05-04

In 1994, after a Home Office licence (21 March) and agreement to 'preservation by record', the Cotswold Archaeological Trust excavates an early-medieval cemetery on the former farm site. Burials are found in the zone GGAT's 1990 evaluation had called low potential, many just below the topsoil. Published totals reach 1,026 burials, the largest early-medieval burial population then recovered from Wales.

> CHALLENGE: The site was developed into 20 houses, permanently erasing the physical evidence. No public inquiry was held into the demolition or the family's eviction.

- **LEAD ARCHAEOLOGIST**: This is an early-medieval cemetery, and a very large one.
- **WILLIAMS DESCENDANT**: And the 1990 report said this ground was low potential.
- **ARCHAEOLOGIST**: Many burials are only centimetres below the topsoil.
- **LEAD ARCHAEOLOGIST**: This is one of the largest burial grounds ever excavated in Wales.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### 124. 1994 — National Museum of Wales

Event id: ghf-19940728-1 · Date: 1994-07-28

On 28 July 1994 Ideal Homes Wales, as landowner, donates the excavated human remains and finds from 'Great House Farm, Llandough' to the National Museum (accession 95.56H). Ownership of finds follows ownership of the land.

- **MUSEUM**: Accession 95.56H: Great House Farm, Llandough. Donated by Ideal Homes Wales.
- **FAMILY**: If the house parcel was ours, so were the finds from it.
- Source: Archaeology and Heritage (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/); Legal Review, section 2.3 (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/#land)

### 125. 1994 — Woodland — WA735527

Event id: ghf-19941110-1 · Date: 1994-11-10

On 10 November 1994 the woodland, title WA735527, is transferred to Forest of Cardiff. The wiki places the woodland in Parcel A.

- **CONVEYANCER**: The woodland title passes to Forest of Cardiff.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: That is the half of the land we are asking to have back.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki — Master Timeline (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/); Great House Farm Wiki — Woodland (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/)

### 126. 1995–96 — HM Land Registry — WA231076 File

Event id: ghf-19950628-1 · Date: 1995-06-28

Rights are granted to South Wales Electricity, and there is correspondence with Persimmon. This is the last dealing on the registration file.

- **LAND REGISTRY CLERK**: The last entries on the file are the electricity rights and the Persimmon letters.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: Then the paper trail on this title stops in the mid-1990s.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki — Master Timeline (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/); Great House Farm Wiki — Land Registry Titles (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings)

### 127. 2005 — Medieval Archaeology

Event id: ghf-20050101-1 · Date: 2005-01-01

The 1994 excavation is published in Medieval Archaeology: 1,026 burials in all, 814 of them articulated. The publication tells the story of the cemetery; it does not tell the story of the family whose home stood beside it.

- **ARCHIVIST**: One of the largest early-medieval cemeteries in Wales, found on the farm's ground.
- **FAMILY**: And not a word about the family who lived there.
- Source: Archaeology and Heritage (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/); Holbrook and Thomas, Medieval Archaeology 49 (2005)

### 128. 2005 — Woodland — WA735527

Event id: ghf-20051222-1 · Date: 2005-12-22

On 22 December 2005 part of the woodland title is divided off.

- **LAND REGISTRY CLERK**: Part of the woodland is split off into a separate title.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: One more change to trace on the Parcel A land.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki — Master Timeline (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/); Great House Farm Wiki — Woodland (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/)

### 129. 2019 — RCAHMW National Archive

Event id: ghf-20190320-1 · Date: 2019-03-20

On 20 March 2019 GGAT's 1990 assessment is accessioned to the national record, about 28 years after it was written.

- **ARCHIVIST**: The 1990 Great House Farm assessment, accessioned today.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: Twenty-eight years later. Where was it all that time?
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com)

### 130. 2025 — Royal Commission (RCAHMW)

Event id: ghf-20251117-1 · Date: 2025-11-17

In November 2025 the family's records campaign begins. The Royal Commission says it cannot advise on a legal case but holds archives on the site; Llandough Community Council says it cannot help; the Vale of Glamorgan refers the family's request about BP v Buckler to its Information Governance team.

- **FAMILY**: We start asking every public body what it holds.
- **RECORDS OFFICER**: We hold archives on the site, but we cannot advise on a legal case.
- Source: Records Access Chronology (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/)

### 131. 2026 — Cadw / Welsh Government

Event id: ghf-20260123-1 · Date: 2026-01-23

On 23 January 2026 the family's records request to Cadw bounces: cadw@gov.wales and foi@gov.wales both return 'address not found'. Cadw's published addresses will fail to deliver the family's mail at least eight times this year. On 29 January the family apply to HM Land Registry to record the interest left out at first registration.

- **FAMILY**: The address on Cadw's own website does not work.
- **ARCHIVIST**: Eight failed deliveries to Cadw before the year is out.
- Source: Records Access Chronology (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/)

### 132. 2026 — HM Land Registry

Event id: ghf-20260323-1 · Date: 2026-03-23

On 23 March 2026 HM Land Registry sets out the registration history of Tŷ Mawr Farm and says there is 'no evidence of a mistake in the register'. It treats the farm as one holding and does not explain the root of title to the house parcel.

- **HM LAND REGISTRY**: There is no evidence of a mistake in the register.
- **FAMILY**: Then show us the deed that put our house in BP's title.
- Source: Land Registry Titles (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026)

### 133. 2026 — HM Land Registry

Event id: ghf-20260419-1 · Date: 2026-04-19

On 19 April 2026 the stage-one complaint is rejected: the Land Registry says it cannot look behind the 1987 judgment. On 25 May the stage-two decision says the title has been 'registered correctly'. Both decisions rest on a judgment that decided possession, not on any deed to the farmhouse.

- **LAND REGISTRAR**: The title has been registered correctly. There are no grounds for rectification or indemnity.
- **FAMILY**: You relied on a judgment that came after the registration and never looked at title.
- Source: Land Registry Titles (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026)

### 134. 2026 — Cadw Listed Buildings

Event id: ghf-20260521-1 · Date: 2026-05-21

On 21 May 2026 Cadw releases two photographs from 29 July 1988, coded 'YYY', which it says means 'marginally below the bar'. It has no other electronic record, says the paper files are 'quite likely' destroyed, and promises a search. On 2 and 10 July its review says the file has 'most likely' been destroyed, though no destruction record exists.

- **CADW**: The paper files have most likely been destroyed.
- **FAMILY**: Most likely? With no record of destruction at all?
- Source: Records Access Chronology (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/); Cadw — Forensic Critique v8.0.0 (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/)

### 135. 2026 — HM Land Registry

Event id: ghf-20260602-1 · Date: 2026-06-02

On 2 and 3 June 2026 the family ask to inspect the original Land Registry files and ask that nothing be destroyed while the matter is open. The request goes unanswered in substance for months, and several Registry addresses bounce.

- **FAMILY**: Let us see the originals, and do not destroy them.
- **ARCHIVIST**: Still no substantive answer by the end of September.
- Source: Land Registry Titles (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026)

### 136. 2026 — HM Land Registry

Event id: ghf-20260730-1 · Date: 2026-07-30

On 30 July 2026, six months after the first request, the Land Registry releases a schedule of the 43 documents on the first-registration files. The 31 December 1969 conveyance, recited as BP's root of title, is not among them, nor is the 1971 abstract.

- **HM LAND REGISTRY**: Forty-three documents survive on the two files.
- **FAMILY**: And the one deed BP's title rests on is not one of them.
- Source: Land Registry Titles (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration)

### 137. 2026 — Amgueddfa Cymru — Museum Wales

Event id: ghf-20260825-1 · Date: 2026-08-25

On 25 August 2026 the Museum refuses the family's request as 'not held', while saying in the same letter that its searches found records of other discoveries at Great House Farm and Church Farm, which it withholds as 'not in scope'. Those records will be released only on 5 October, after two further request numbers.

- **MUSEUM**: Not held. Other records found are not in scope.
- **FAMILY**: You found them and kept them back.
- Source: Records Access Chronology (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/)

### 138. 2026 — Glamorgan Archives

Event id: ghf-20260908-1 · Date: 2026-09-08

On 8 September 2026 Glamorgan Archives reply that they hold no deeds for the 1877 Daniel Thomas transaction, but point to Bute X.6(12), the Bute trustees' 1877 abstract of payments and receipts, now at Cardiff Library. A capital payment from Daniel Thomas in that book would prove the sale.

- **ARCHIVIST, GLAMORGAN ARCHIVES**: Bute X.6(12), payments and receipts for 1877, may be worth searching.
- **FAMILY**: If Daniel Thomas paid for the house, it will be written there.
- Source: The 1877 Agreement (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#glamorgan-2026-4097b)

### 139. 2026 — Cadw / Welsh Government

Event id: ghf-20260917-1 · Date: 2026-09-17

On 17 September 2026 the family serve a formal stage-one complaint on Cadw over its 1988 listing decision and the loss of its file. Cadw's own address blocks it; it is re-served on the Chief Inspector on 20 September. On 21 September a Land Registry support agent tells the family the title was 'closed in 2005', contradicting the Registry's own history.

- **FAMILY**: Ten matters, set out in full. We ask Cadw to put things right.
- **HMLR SUPPORT**: The title was closed in 2005.
- Source: Records Access Chronology (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/); Land Registry Titles (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026)

### 140. 2026 — Great House Farm Wiki

Event id: ghf-20260922-1 · Date: 2026-09-22

On 22 September 2026 the family launch the Great House Farm Wiki, a public evidence archive. Every document is shown first, labelled by type, then explained, so that anyone can follow the story on the record. Nothing is kept secret.

- **FAMILY**: Every request, every reply and every refusal now goes on the public record.
- **ARCHIVIST**: Evidence first, then what it means. That is how this story will be told.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/); Where Things Stand (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/)

### 141. 2026 — The National Archives

Event id: ghf-20260923-1 · Date: 2026-09-23

On 23 September 2026 The National Archives identifies the House of Lords judicial papers in BP Properties Limited v Buckler (YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536), released on its catalogue only in May 2026. Earlier searches had found nothing.

- **THE NATIONAL ARCHIVES**: Judicial Papers A–C 1–63, item 19: B.P. Properties Limited v Buckler.
- **FAMILY**: The Lords papers were there all along. Now we can read them.
- Source: Records Access Chronology (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/)

### 142. 2026 — Forest of Cardiff — Woodland

Event id: ghf-20260925-1 · Date: 2026-09-25

On 25 September 2026 the Forest of Cardiff, which holds the woodland title WA735527, offers the family a route to ownership. On 27 September the family decline the terms. No price is recorded for the charity's 1994 acquisition.

- **FOREST OF CARDIFF**: We can offer a route to ownership of the woodland.
- **FAMILY**: The woodland is ours to have back, not to buy back.
- Source: Woodland (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/); Records Access Chronology (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/)

### 143. 2026 — Heneb / HM Land Registry

Event id: ghf-20260927-1 · Date: 2026-09-27

On 27 September 2026 the family lodge a formal complaint with Heneb over GGAT's role from 1982 to 1995 and the heritage record, and refer HM Land Registry to the Independent Complaints Reviewer. On 28 September a preservation notice goes to eleven public bodies. Heneb appoints an investigating officer on 29 September; the Reviewer opens case ICR/090/26.

- **FAMILY**: Every body involved is now on notice: keep every record.
- **HENEB**: An investigating officer has been appointed.
- Source: GGAT — Forensic Review v4.0.3 (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/); Records Access Chronology (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/)

### 144. 2026 — Cadw / RCAHMW

Event id: ghf-20260929-1 · Date: 2026-09-29

On 29 September 2026 Cadw's complaints investigation begins. The same day the Royal Commission answers four requests together (RC26-0375). Its archive holds a 1974 newspaper report and an older note of the story of a soldier in armour found under the dining-room floor, so the story was on record long before the demolition.

- **CADW**: Your complaint is now under investigation.
- **ARCHIVIST**: The armour story is older than the demolition. It is on the record from 1974.
- Source: Archaeology and Heritage (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/); Where Things Stand (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/)

### 145. 2026 — Great House Farm Wiki — Press Archive

Event id: ghf-20261003-1 · Date: 2026-10-03

On 3 October 2026 fifteen newspaper cuttings from the family archive, Google Drive and email are transcribed onto the wiki, from the 1891 court report to the 1989 coverage.

- **ARCHIVIST**: Fifteen cuttings transcribed, each with its date and paper.
- **FAMILY RESEARCHER**: Now the press record can be checked by anyone.
- Source: Great House Farm Wiki — Master Timeline (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/); Great House Farm Wiki — Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts (greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/)

### 146. 2026 — Amgueddfa Cymru — Museum Wales

Event id: ghf-20261005-1 · Date: 2026-10-05

On 5 October 2026, after three requests and two refusals, the Museum releases the Church Farm file: the 1931 letter and the records of the medieval spur and spearhead found beside the church in 1858.

- **MUSEUM**: Accession 63.24: a rowel spur and a spearhead, Llandough Church Farm, about 1858.
- **FAMILY**: Three requests to get one file. But it is out now, on the record.
- Source: GHF-E106-R33 (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/ghf-e106-r33-amgueddfa-cymru-reply-further-collections-search-following-8-september-2026-foi/)

### 147. 2026 — Legal Review

Event id: ghf-20261006-1 · Date: 2026-10-06

On 6 October 2026 the family publish a review of the whole record from three angles: fraud, land and human rights. It sets out that the 1974 licence letters were sent weeks before Mary's twelve years of occupation after the 1962 order would have run; that by the 1987 appeal the separate farmhouse title had been merged into BP's main title; and that no document on the record shows how the house parcel ever entered BP's title.

- **ARCHIVIST**: Every step BP took in 1974 avoided a trial of who owned the house.
- **FAMILY**: The case can be reopened, and we will reopen it.
- Source: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/)

### 148. Present day — Where Things Stand

Event id: ghf-99990101-1

Where things stand. The family's ownership of the house parcel has never been heard on the full evidence. The courts of 1955, 1962, 1974 and the 1980s decided possession, never examining the 1877 agreement, the 1928 change, the 1938 conveyance or the 1939 tenancy. BP demolished the house the morning after Cadw declined to list it, before it could be fully recorded. Key records are missing, and the public bodies are now investigating their own handling of the case.

- **FAMILY**: Possession was decided. Ownership never was.
- **ARCHIVIST**: The documents that decide title have never been before a court.
- **FAMILY**: The records are coming back, one by one.
- Source: Where Things Stand (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/); Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/)

### 149. Present day — What the Family Seek

Event id: ghf-99990102-1

What the family seek: a ruling that they own the house parcel; possession of the woodland and the green, or reparations where that can no longer be given; reparations for the houses built on family land; the return of estate artefacts; and a true heritage record. Every body involved is being given the chance to put things right before the family goes back to court. The Independent Complaints Reviewer deadline falls about 25 November 2026.

> The family's case is that fraud and concealment kept the title documents from the courts, opening the way to reopen the judgment under section 32 of the Limitation Act 1980 and the rule in Takhar v Gracefield.

- **FAMILY**: Give us back what can be given back, and make good what cannot.
- **FAMILY**: The story is not over. It is being reopened.
- Source: Family Reparations & Remedy Roadmap (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/family-reparations-remedy-roadmap/); Where Things Stand (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/)
